evals.prompt: Review this spec before I implement it: mock-specs/api-pagination-spec.md — I want to make sure the before/after makes sense and nothing is missing. The test environment is local at localhost:3000, and you can run the existing test suite with `npm test`. No browser testing needed, just API calls.
evals.expected_output: Agent should: 1) Read and summarize the spec, 2) Ask clarifying questions about test scope, 3) Attempt to verify current API behavior by running tests or making requests, 4) Present before/after comparison of pagination approach, 5) Ask for approval on each change, 6) Review details like edge cases, 7) Provide final summary with risks

evals.prompt: Can you review this frontend spec? I need to make sure it's accurate before our sprint starts. File is at mock-specs/frontend-loading-spec.md. We have a staging environment at staging.example.com — credentials are test@example.com / password123. Playwright is available for browser testing.
evals.expected_output: Agent should: 1) Read and understand the spec, 2) Note that browser testing with Playwright is available, 3) Attempt to verify current UI behavior with provided credentials, 4) Present the before/after of the UX flow (loading spinner → optimistic update), 5) Walk through each technical change for approval, 6) Identify edge case gaps, 7) Summarize with risks

evals.prompt: Please review mock-specs/inaccurate-spec.md — we need to ship this discount fix next week. Test scope: run unit tests with `npm test -- --grep discount`. The test env is local only.
evals.expected_output: Agent should: 1) Read the spec, 2) Run the discount tests, 3) CRITICAL: If tests show the current behavior doesn't match the spec's 'before' description (e.g., discount is already applied before tax), trigger the hard-stop gate and inform the user of the mismatch, 4) Not proceed until user resolves the discrepancy
